case_name: G. Sagar Suri and Another v State of Uttar Pradesh and Others

statutes.act: Code Or Article 227 Of The Constitution

facts: The appellants had sought quashing of criminal proceedings pending against them under Section 406/420 of the Indian Penal Code.
A First Information Report (FIR) was filed against seven persons, including the two appellants, by Mr. P.K. Sen Gupta, General Manager, M/s. Phoenix International Finance Ltd.
The FIR alleged that the accused persons had cheated and committed fraud on the complainant's company.
The Police registered a case against four persons, namely, G. Sagar Suri, Shama Suri, Ashwani Suri, and Shalini Suri, describing them as Directors of M/s. Ganga Automobiles Ltd.
The complainant had already instituted a complaint under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act in the Court of the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Ghaziabad.
issues: Whether the criminal proceedings pending against the appellants can be quashed?
petitioner_arguments: The appellants argued that the criminal proceedings were based on a false and fabricated FIR.
They contended that the complainant had no locus standi to file the FIR.
respondent_arguments: The respondent argued that the FIR was genuine and the accused persons had committed fraud and cheated the complainant's company.
court_reasoning: The court held that the FIR was not fabricated and the accused persons had indeed committed fraud and cheated the complainant's company.
The court noted that the appellants had failed to establish any material irregularity in the investigation or the filing of the FIR.
holding: The appeal was dismissed, and the criminal proceedings pending against the appellants were allowed to continue.
